requirements.requirement: The plant and clock reproduce the same event sequence for a fixed configuration, seed, and fault schedule.
requirements.acceptance: Compare canonical JSON event hashes across two runs; exclude wall-clock metadata.
requirements.rationale: An intermittent failure is actionable only if the inputs and event order can be reproduced.

requirements.requirement: Sensors carry unit, sample time, receive time, quality, and provenance separately.
requirements.acceptance: Delay and replay packets; verify sample age is unchanged and unit mismatch is rejected.
requirements.rationale: Unit errors and confused sampling/receipt timestamps can invalidate otherwise correct control decisions.

requirements.requirement: Arming, starting, stopping, and recovery follow the specified state graph.
requirements.acceptance: Table-test every state/event pair, including illegal starts and simultaneous stop/start.
requirements.rationale: An explicit transition table makes illegal starts and recovery paths reviewable.

requirements.requirement: Stale age >200 ms and future timestamps are detected using sample time.
requirements.acceptance: Test 199, 200, 201 ms ages and future timestamps; receiving an old packet cannot reset freshness.
requirements.rationale: A delayed packet must not make stale sensor data appear fresh.

requirements.requirement: A detected fault commands pump off and valve open within 10 ms.
requirements.acceptance: Independent event monitor measures detection-to-command latency under all fault schedules.
requirements.rationale: A fault response needs a measurable deadline; issuing a command is distinct from reaching a physical state.

requirements.requirement: Reconnect cannot restart the stand and fault history remains latched.
requirements.acceptance: Disconnect during a run, reconnect, acknowledge, rearm; missing any recovery step blocks start.
requirements.rationale: Reconnect is transport recovery, not authorization to resume a potentially hazardous process.

requirements.requirement: Expired and conflicting duplicate commands are rejected; exact duplicates are not reapplied.
requirements.acceptance: Vary expiry around 100 ms and repeat IDs with identical and changed payloads.
requirements.rationale: Delayed or repeated messages must not produce duplicate or outdated actions.

requirements.requirement: All five fault types are injected deterministically and detected under their specified conditions.
requirements.acceptance: Scenario manifest includes onset, values, expected earliest detection, and exact required response.
requirements.rationale: Each failure mode needs an independently specified onset and response.

requirements.requirement: The monitor catches six seeded controller defects without using controller implementation logic.
requirements.acceptance: Freshness from receive time, inverted valve command, pressure unit mismatch, unsafe reconnect, unbounded retry, and lost latch each fail.
requirements.rationale: Deliberate controller defects test the monitor rather than merely the happy-path controller.

requirements.requirement: Run artifacts preserve hashes and identify interrupted runs as incomplete.
requirements.acceptance: Interrupt recording, corrupt an artifact, and reproduce a completed run from its manifest.
requirements.rationale: A partial or corrupted trace cannot justify a successful run.

requirements.requirement: Recipe validation and randomized event sequences preserve the invariant set.
requirements.acceptance: Reject nonfinite values and unknown units; run 1000 bounded Hypothesis sequences and store counterexamples.
requirements.rationale: Sequences expose ordering bugs that isolated state tests miss.

requirements.requirement: Offline demo and report work without hardware or credentials and disclose the simulation boundary.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh-install run verifies charts, fault times, and labels; all twelve invariants have assertions.
requirements.rationale: An engineer should be able to inspect the timeline without building a physical stand.

requirements.requirement: Compare pytest plus RTAMT and OpenHTF against the required replay and timing workflow before introducing a new framework.
requirements.rationale: The useful contribution must be integration or clearer engineering evidence, not reimplementing test execution or temporal logic.
requirements.acceptance: Use one stale-input and one reconnect scenario; document installed versions, configuration, timestamp semantics, reporting gaps, and reuse choices in docs/BASELINE.md. Prefer a small adapter/recipe library if existing tools satisfy the requirements.

requirements.requirement: Import versioned JSONL traces and CSV through an explicit column/unit map without running the bundled plant.
requirements.rationale: Real engineers already have logs; requiring the pump simulator would make the tool a demonstration only.
requirements.acceptance: A separately authored trace produces the same verdict through both formats. Preserve raw sample and receive times; reject ambiguous units, missing required channels, and unsupported clock relationships.

requirements.requirement: A public Python controller adapter accepts measurements and a virtual tick and returns commands; pytest can invoke the runner without a web server.
requirements.rationale: An engineer needs to test their controller, not only the bundled implementation.
requirements.acceptance: A controller in a separate consumer directory runs without editing abyssbench source. Its command stream is judged by the independent monitor; no controller helper is imported into expected-value calculations.

requirements.requirement: Temporal verdicts are pass, fail, or inconclusive and state their observation window and clock assumptions.
requirements.rationale: Incomplete traces and incompatible clocks are common sources of false assurance.
requirements.acceptance: A trace ending before a response deadline is inconclusive, never pass. Missing sample time cannot prove freshness. Reject unordered sequence IDs and unsupported cross-clock timestamps; check exact threshold boundaries. Streaming future-window rules remain pending until their deadlines.

requirements.requirement: Reuse the same monitor and trace interface in a second, simple thermal-controller example with stale-temperature and heater-off requirements.
requirements.rationale: A second domain is a concrete test that the public abstraction is reusable rather than hard-coded to a pump.
requirements.acceptance: Freeze a separate example specification with valid, violating, and incomplete traces. Configure channels and rules without changing the monitor engine or importing fluid-model code.

requirements.requirement: Provide an OpenHTF integration example and optional Parquet export after the JSONL/pytest workflow works.
requirements.rationale: This helps adoption in an existing station workflow but is not needed to prove the core tool.
requirements.acceptance: The integration attaches requirement verdicts and artifacts to a test record; Parquet and JSONL retain identical timestamps and units.
requirements.applies_when: If selected after Must requirements pass

requirements.requirement: Publish a versioned input and result schema, stable requirement IDs, public Python API, and a scriptable CLI with clear failure semantics.
requirements.rationale: CI must not confuse an unsupported check or crashed evaluator with a valid result.
requirements.acceptance: For normal check commands: exit 0 only when every applicable required check passes; exit 1 for violations; exit 2 for invalid, incomplete, unsupported, or failed execution. Results preserve individual pass/fail/inconclusive/not_applicable states. The demo command separately verifies its expected negative cases. Unknown schema versions are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Declare resource limits and measure repeatable performance for the supported workload in the pinned environment.
requirements.rationale: A tool that hangs or silently drops large input cannot be trusted in an engineering workflow.
requirements.acceptance: During M0 freeze input-size/case limits and a target runtime with machine details. M4 records actual elapsed time and peak memory; an oversized input or elapsed-time limit produces a bounded error and incomplete result. CAD work runs in a killable worker. Compare against the baseline; do not claim universal performance.

requirements.requirement: Keep offline workflows local by default and document dependency, fixture, manual, and example licensing.
requirements.rationale: Engineers must be able to inspect data handling and legally reuse the code and examples.
requirements.acceptance: No credentials or telemetry are needed; the offline demo completes with egress disabled after installation. Source examples have provenance and redistributable licenses, or use a download recipe and lawful independently authored fixtures. Escape user text in HTML; reject output path traversal and avoid executing input data.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate adoption from a separate clean consumer directory using only the documented public interface.
requirements.rationale: A successful bundled demo alone is not evidence that another engineer can use the tool.
requirements.acceptance: Record a complete cold-start walkthrough: install, configure one non-default input, get an expected failure, correct it, and reproduce success without editing package source. Include actual commands, setup time, code/config size, and limitations versus the baseline. Label agent-executed walkthroughs as such; practitioner validation remains unverified until real feedback exists.

exclusions.requirement: A replacement for OpenHTF, labgrid, RTAMT, or a production SCADA system
exclusions.rationale: Existing projects solve those broader problems; scope is replay and engineering contracts.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: A calibrated hydraulic model, digital twin, or prediction of real process performance
exclusions.rationale: The reference equations are deliberately illustrative and unvalidated.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Functional safety certification, hard real-time guarantees, or automatic control of a live stand
exclusions.rationale: Software simulation evidence does not qualify a deployed control system.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: A custom temporal-logic language or theorem prover
exclusions.rationale: Start with a small explicit rule schema; evaluate existing monitoring libraries.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

exclusions.requirement: Distributed multi-clock reconstruction, arbitrary PLC adapters, and C++ in the first release
exclusions.rationale: These introduce separate synchronization/toolchain problems; the first external controller interface is Python.
exclusions.acceptance: Absent from the v1 supported-features list; README and reports do not claim this capability.

priority_policy.should: Valuable after Must; omission needs an explicit rationale
